newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya recalls U.S. envoy after political gaffe.
newsitem.headline: Kenya recalls U.S. envoy after political gaffe.

text.p: Kenya has recalled its ambassador to the United States after a major political gaffe, the foreign ministry and diplomatic sources said on Friday.
A Kenyan foreign ministry statement said Benjamin Kipkorir had been recalled at the end of his tour of duty on July 31 and gave no further details.
But diplomats said Kipkorir was removed as ambassador after an embarrassing episode over constitutional reform in Kenya.

In what the Kenyan embassy in Washington described as a mix-up, Kipkorir presented to a U.S. Congress sub-committee draft bills on constitutional reform from an opposition parliament member instead of drafts from the attorney-general.
Attorney-General Amos Wako told reporters this week that Kipkorir presented the wrong documents "and we don't know what the source of his documents was and why he did not verify."
The foreign ministry said Samuel Chemai would become the new Kenyan ambassador to the United States, also responsible for Colombia and Mexico. Chemai moves from Japan.

Constitutional reforms have been a thorny subject in Kenya. An opposition-backed alliance pressing for such reforms before elections this year has called a general strike in Kenya on Friday. Protest rallies the alliance called in July ended in violence, with at least nine people killed.
